html:
The Yirandhali were an Aboriginal Australian people of north Queensland, in the area of today's Shire of Flinders around Hughenden, on the upper Flinders River.

Little is recorded about them. Their country was open grassland with the river and its waterholes as the lifeline. Neighbours included the Yilba, Mbara, Miyan and Iningai. Sheep and cattle stations took the Flinders grasslands from the early 1860s, and Hughenden grew from one of them.
sum: The Yirandhali were an Aboriginal Australian people of north Queensland, in the area of today's Shire of Flinders around Hughenden, on the upper Flinders River.
